Paired fixed-data preprocessing pilot

Whitening reveals c information, but calibration remains incomplete

ZCA improves c median RMSE from 0.4420 to 0.1697 in this controlled pilot. But all six ZCA SBC screens fail: nominal 90% intervals cover only 54.9–60.9% of physical truths and 74.0% of c truths. This small fixed-data estimator is not calibrated or accepted for use.

The nominal central credible level is 90%. The same 512 validation truths and noisy observations are used in both arms. Better point recovery and narrower intervals do not establish a calibrated posterior. These prior-predictive SBC screens adjust over six marginals within an arm; the pilot provides no release acceptance family.

All six marginal rank ECDF deviations. Calibration problems are visible even when medians follow the unit line.

PNG · SVG

What the input covariance means

xᵢ=Yᵢ/hᵢ;   Σᵢⱼ=mean-training covariance of feature i with feature j

Each row is a simulated 54-quote surface; each column is one fixed option quote divided by its half-spread. A common change in volatility level, skew or maturity shape moves many columns together. Σ is estimated across the 10,000 noisy training rows and measures that shared variation, including variation from the physical-parameter prior and quote noise.

Yᵢ=Pᵢ(φ)+c hᵢ Zᵢ,   Zᵢ∼N(0,1)

The observation model and priors stay fixed. Both networks infer all five Heston parameters and c jointly. The preprocessing changes their numerical input representation while retaining all 54 features.

Diagonal preprocessing subtracts the fitted mean and divides each feature by its training standard deviation. Full ZCA also uses off-diagonal covariance: if Σ=Q diag(λ) Qᵀ, its symmetric matrix is W=Q diag(max(λ,10⁻⁸λmax)⁻¹ᐟ²) Qᵀ and the network receives (x−mean)W. The eigenvalue floor bounds amplification; no eigenvector is discarded. The mean and matrix are fitted in float64 on training only, saved as an immutable sidecar, reused once for validation/inference, and then cast to float32.

Both arms use the same noisy training covariance. Diagonal scaling leaves strong dependence; ZCA brings the full fitted covariance close to identity. The declared floor clips 0 eigenvalues in this run.

Controlled training recipe

Input transformc median RMSE · 512c truth–median correlationMedian c 90% widthSBC screens
Fixed diagonal0.44203-0.00121.33843/6
Fixed ZCA0.1697+0.92330.365350/6

Both fresh bounded-target BayesFlow 2.1 spline CouplingFlows use depth 6, 128×128 conditioners, zero dropout, identical trainable initialization, the same fixed10,000 noisy rows, batch 256 and 200 passes: 8000 updates and 2m presentations. Both use the same seeded permutations and unpadded 16-row tails. Adam follows CosineDecay(5e−4,8000,alpha=.1), ending at 5e−5. Only targets have BayesFlow running standardization; input transforms are frozen before training. All six targets retain their declared bounded transformations and priors.

The losses use 512 fixed training probes and 100 fixed validation probes. The separate final recovery/SBC population has 512 cases. A widening training/validation gap is evidence to examine before scaling or accepting this small fixed-data fit.

PNG · SVG

The source notebook also changes to FlowMatching with three 128-unit layers, dropout .1 and raw unconstrained targets. This pilot tests its whitening idea while holding the two new arms’ network and training recipe fixed. Historical 500-pass networks used a warm start, 100k physical rows and fresh c/noise on every pass with 50m examples; their saved results below are context, not matched controls for this small fresh fit.

Parameterwise recovery

All 512 posterior medians and 90% intervals for 32 fixed-index rows per arm. Unit-line alignment measures point recovery; the coverage/SBC table above evaluates uncertainty.

Data boundaries and source evidence

Both fit-condition hashes, target hashes and row hashes match. Preprocessing sees training rows only. The raw evaluation conditions and truths match the historical 512-case population exactly. Sidecars are bundled with each native checkpoint and checked by source/task/data hashes before sampling. No reserved data, new labels, new reference sampling, grid redesign or Bergomi changes enter this pilot.
